ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, it is known that $\odot O$ is the circumscribed circle of quadrilateral $ABCD$ with $O$ as the center of the circle. If $\angle BCD=120^\circ$ and $AB=AD=2\, \text{cm}$, then what is the length of the radius of $\odot O$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw BD and construct OE $\perp$ AD at E, and draw OD.\\
Since $\odot O$ is the circumcircle of quadrilateral ABCD, and $\angle BCD=120^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle BAD=60^\circ$.\\
Given AD=AB=2cm,\\
triangle ABD is an equilateral triangle.\\
Hence, DE= $\frac{1}{2}$ AD=1cm, and $\angle ODE= \frac{1}{2} \angle ADB=30^\circ$,\\
therefore, OD= $\frac{DE}{\cos 30^\circ}$ = $\boxed{\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}}$ cm.
